print-through-n.explanation: range stops before its second argument, so n + 1 includes n. When n is zero, the loop has no iterations. The colon starts the loop body.

sum-array.explanation: Start the running total at zero and add each value once. An empty list leaves the result at zero.

reverse-string.explanation: A slice with step -1 visits characters from the end to the beginning. Case and spaces stay unchanged.
reverse-string.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for the returned string.

find-largest.explanation: Initialize with an actual element, rather than zero, so all-negative inputs work. Keep the largest element seen so far.
find-largest.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) temporary space for the slice in this implementation.

count-vowels.code:
def solve(text):
    return sum(1 for char in text.lower() if char in 'aeiou')
count-vowels.explanation: Lowercase the text, then count characters in the five ASCII vowels defined by this problem.
count-vowels.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for the lowercase string.

binary-search.explanation: The possible answer stays inside the inclusive interval [left, right]. Each comparison discards the middle element and one half. An empty interval means the target is absent.
binary-search.complexity: O(log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space.

palindrome.explanation: Compare symmetric characters and move toward the center. This problem compares case and spaces exactly; it does not remove punctuation.

balanced-brackets.explanation: The most recent unclosed bracket must match the next closing bracket. A stack records that order. Any leftover opening brackets make the input invalid.
balanced-brackets.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.

factorial.explanation: Zero and one are base cases with result one. Otherwise multiply n by the factorial of n - 1. Inputs are restricted to nonnegative small integers.
factorial.complexity: O(n) recursive calls and O(n) call-stack space under the small-integer cost model.

max-subarray.explanation: At each element, either extend the previous segment or start a new one. Track the best segment anywhere. Initializing from the first element handles all-negative lists.
max-subarray.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) temporary space for the slice in this implementation.

unique-window.explanation: Maintain a window with no repeated characters. When a character repeats inside it, move left past its previous position. max prevents the left boundary from moving backward.
unique-window.complexity: O(n) expected time and O(k) space, where k is the number of distinct characters.

stair-ways.explanation: A path reaching step n ends with a one-step move from n - 1 or a two-step move from n - 2. Add those counts. The zero-step case has one empty path.
stair-ways.complexity: O(n) additions and O(1) integer variables; integer arithmetic grows with n.

lc-two-sum.explanation: Use a map from number to index to locate the complement.

lc-binary-search.code:
def solve(nums, target):
    lo, hi = 0, len(nums)-1
    while lo <= hi:
        mid = (lo+hi)//2
        if nums[mid] == target: return mid
        if nums[mid] < target: lo = mid+1
        else: hi = mid-1
    return -1
lc-binary-search.explanation: Discard the half that cannot contain the target.

lc-valid-parentheses.explanation: A stack checks the most recent unmatched opening bracket.

lc-palindrome-number.code:
def solve(x):
    return x >= 0 and str(x) == str(x)[::-1]
lc-palindrome-number.explanation: Compare the nonnegative decimal representation with its reverse.

lc-length-of-last-word.explanation: Split on whitespace and count the final word.

lc-single-number.code:
def solve(nums):
    value=0
    for n in nums: value ^= n
    return value
lc-single-number.explanation: XOR cancels pairs; the unpaired value remains.

lc-contains-duplicate.explanation: A set removes duplicates, reducing the length if any occur.

lc-search-insert-position.code:
def solve(nums, target):
    lo, hi = 0, len(nums)
    while lo < hi:
        mid=(lo+hi)//2
        if nums[mid] < target: lo=mid+1
        else: hi=mid
    return lo
lc-search-insert-position.explanation: Find the first position whose value is at least the target.

lc-sqrtx.explanation: The integer square root is exact and avoids floating-point rounding.
lc-sqrtx.complexity: Depends on integer arithmetic; no floating-point conversion

lc-climbing-stairs.code:
def solve(n):
    a,b=1,1
    for _ in range(n): a,b=b,a+b
    return a
lc-climbing-stairs.explanation: Each step count combines the counts from one and two steps earlier.

lc-best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.code:
def solve(prices):
    low=prices[0]
    best=0
    for price in prices:
        best=max(best,price-low)
        low=min(low,price)
    return best
lc-best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.explanation: Track the lowest earlier price and best single-sale profit.

lc-maximum-subarray.explanation: Kadane's algorithm chooses between extending or restarting a subarray.

lc-longest-common-prefix.explanation: Shorten the candidate prefix until every string begins with it.
